answer: Refractory cooldowns resist sybils: after a consequential action an identity enters a mandatory rest period before it can act again, so each account's throughput is hard-capped per unit time. A swarm gains aggregate rate only by holding MORE aged, established identities — not by spamming — because every fake falls into the same hollow cooldown after one move. An attacker cannot compress a flood into an instant; the basalt-hard refractory window spreads any attack thin across real elapsed time, umber-slow.
